feature.summary: Planned connections to licensed research, shopping, bookings, media playback and messaging apps (iMessage, SMS, WhatsApp, Telegram). No finished connector exists for any of them. The directory lists some vendors, but the release gate keeps them off, and the messaging catalog entries cannot be connected. Native messaging code was not found.

purpose.what_it_does: Nothing is promised to users yet. The aim is for the assistant to retrieve licensed research, look up products, make bookings, control media and read or send messages through connected services.
purpose.why_it_exists: ChatGPT and Claude are moving toward consumer actions; the brief lists these as wave 3 items that are not built (doc: audit/partial/056-concrete-integration-families.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: No one today. Intended for consumers on paid managed plans.
problems_solved: Future: ordering, booking and messaging from chat.
Future: reading licensed research the user already pays for.
use_cases: Future: 'book a table for two on Friday'.
Future: 'send this to Sam on WhatsApp'.
Future: 'summarise the licensed report I have access to'.

where_to_find_it: Web, Desktop (hosted web) and Mobile: the connector directory may list vendors such as Booking.com, Expedia, Spotify, Instacart, Taskrabbit and Twilio from a vendor snapshot (apps/web/lib/connectors/directory/sources/vendor-directory.json); they read 'Coming soon' while unreleased (mobile index.tsx:162-164).
Web Connectors settings catalog lists Telegram, WhatsApp and Twilio as api-key entries (apps/web/features/connectors/data/connectors.ts:637-662).
prerequisites: None can be met: no working connector exists in the code read.
screens_and_controls: Directory cards that read 'Coming soon' or show a setup message such as 'has no remote MCP server this deployment can reach' (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-setup.ts:155-162).
journey: A person browsing Connectors sees a vendor card.
They cannot connect it; the card says Coming soon or setup is needed.
Asking the assistant for the action reaches no connector tool.
feedback_and_outputs: Setup requirement message from the server.

working: Directory listing and 'Coming soon' labelling for these vendors exist as part of the general connector directory (apps/web/lib/connectors/directory/; mobile index.tsx:162).
General custom remote MCP connectors exist, which could reach a vendor that publishes an MCP server, but they are blocked by the release gate today (user-connector-tools.ts:2491-2493).
incomplete: Telegram, WhatsApp and Twilio are catalog entries with api-key auth (catalog.ts:226-228) but no MCP endpoint, so describeConnectorSetup reports no remote server (oauth-setup.ts:155-162).
The vendor snapshot lists Booking.com, Expedia, Spotify, Instacart and Taskrabbit with MCP URLs, but nothing in AGI declares tool metadata or approval rules for booking, purchase or playback actions.
disconnected_or_disabled: All of these ids are outside the 13 released connectors (connector-release.ts:16-30), so their tools never reach a turn.
not_available: Native messaging (iMessage, SMS, WhatsApp, Telegram): no integration code found in apps, packages or crates (searched for iMessage; the only matches were unrelated names ending in UiMessage).
Licensed research retrieval: no connector or tool found; PitchBook appears in the vendor snapshot with no MCP URL.
Media playback: Spotify appears in the snapshot with a pilot gateway URL only; no tool code.
All apps: CLI and VS Code have no connector of their own.

established.statement: The assistant can retrieve content from licensed research sources through a connected account.
The assistant can look up products and prices through a connected shopping service.
The assistant can search for and make reservations or bookings through a connected service.
The assistant can control media playback in a connected media service.
The assistant can read or send messages in native messaging apps on the user's behalf.
Connectors stay 'coming soon' until the release state changes.

acceptance_criteria: No page, label or assistant answer claims that bookings, shopping, playback or messaging work.
Directory cards for these vendors cannot be connected while unreleased.
Asking the assistant to send a WhatsApp message does not run any connector tool and the assistant says it cannot.
Any future build declares tool metadata (read or external send) before it can be offered.
A future messaging or booking send always asks for approval and is irreversible-class (matches tool-metadata.ts external_send rules).
inferred: Anything that sends a message, books or buys is an external send or irreversible write and must ask every time [inferred from tool-metadata.ts:933-939 risk tiers].
proposed: [proposed] Write a design and approval rules per family before any build, as the brief row states.
[proposed] Keep these ids out of public copy until released.

corrections.claim: General custom remote MCP connectors exist ... but they are blocked by the release gate today (user-connector-tools.ts:2491-2493).
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Lines 2491-2493 are the first checks in dialPermitted (connectorReleased(serverId) false -> not permitted). Custom connectors reach it at 2598 (customServerId, member=true), org-shared at 2618, and 2581. The block holds because custom ids are not in the 13-id list, but the cited lines do not mention custom connectors.
corrections.correction: Custom remote MCP connectors are dropped because dialPermitted calls connectorReleased on their custom or org-shared server ids (user-connector-tools.ts:2491, 2598, 2618), and those ids are not among the 13 released ids.

corrections.claim: The server builds the listing and marks the entry unavailable or needs-setup (connectable.ts:9-30).
corrections.what_the_code_shows: connectable.ts:9-14 returns 'desktop-and-cli', 'connect', 'unavailable' or 'needs-setup'. It never reads the release gate, so a catalog entry with an endpoint returns 'connect' whether released or not. Lines 16-30 return 'desktop-and-cli', 'connect', 'needs-setup' or 'api-key-form'. 'Coming soon' is applied client-side from connectorReleased (mobile index.tsx:162).
corrections.correction: The server computes only the connectable mode and ignores the release gate. The Coming soon label is applied on the client from connectorReleased.

corrections.claim: Unreleased vendor: Card reads 'Coming soon'; no connect (mobile index.tsx:162-164).
corrections.what_the_code_shows: index.tsx:162 sets comingSoon = !row.connection && !connectorReleased(row.routeId); 163 uses it only for the detail text, and the accessibility label at ~168-170. The row still has onPress. These lines do not show that connecting is blocked.
corrections.correction: Unreleased, unconnected rows show the Coming soon label (index.tsx:162-163). Blocking of connect is not shown at these lines; check the onPress handler.

corrections.claim: Limits and metering: none found in the code.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Per-plan connector tool caps exist: maxConnectorTools is 0 on one plan (line 626) and 50/150/500/unlimited/custom on others, read by getPlanMaxConnectorTools (812-813). resolveConnectorToolLimit is used at user-connector-tools.ts:2441. General, not service-specific, but they apply.
corrections.correction: Connector tools are capped per plan by maxConnectorTools (billing-catalog.ts:571-722). No service-specific limit exists.

missing_facts: Telegram, WhatsApp and Twilio already have declared risk classes (telegram read-write, whatsapp and twilio high-impact) and display names. The page's claim that nothing declares approval rules overlooks this pre-wired classification: apps/web/lib/connectors/mcp-endpoints.ts:117-119,220-221.
Plan limits apply to connectors: maxConnectorTools caps per plan (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:571-722,812-813), contradicting the 'none found' limits row.

The web Settings catalog gives telegram, whatsapp and twilio a build phase (3 or 4) and capability summaries such as 'message sending' (apps/web/features/connectors/data/connectors.ts:637-662), which can read as promises while the gate and missing endpoint block connecting.
